editorial:
Imagine you are stuck working a wedding where everything that can go wrong actually does. That is exactly where you find Jim, a stressed-out banquet server in New Hampshire. He is just trying to survive the night by following a strict set of rules called the Ten Commandments of Banquet Serving. The whole vibe is chaotic and funny, throwing you right into a world of violent florists, confused old people, and a Mother of the Bride who looks like she wants to kill someone. It feels like a fever dream where the stakes are surprisingly high for a party.

The animation style is quirky and fits the crazy energy of the plot. You will love how the pacing never lets up, making the wedding feel like a battlefield. While some of the jokes are a bit wild, the humor mostly hits the mark. If you have ever worked in food service, you will relate to this on a deep level. You should definitely check this out by streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Jim barely surviving the wedding chaos. After facing off against the scary Mother of the Bride and the angry florists, he finally completes his shift. The big twist is that following the rules didn't actually save him from the madness, but it gave him the sanity to get through it. He finishes the night exhausted but proud, proving that he can handle any disaster as long as he has his list.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves workplace comedies and weird animation.
